Easy-Hard Balanced Accuracy

Source: R/metric_difficulty.R
metric_easy_hard_accuracy.Rd

Computes accuracy within each difficulty stratum (easy/hard) and returns their mean. This rewards panels that perform well on hard-to-classify samples rather than relying on easy cases to inflate overall accuracy.

metric_easy_hard_accuracy(
  truth,
  scores = NULL,
  selected = NULL,
  difficulty = NULL,
  cutoff_prob = 0.5,
  cutoff_strategy = c("fixed", "prevalence", "youden"),
  positive = "Yes"
)

Arguments

truth

Binary outcome; coerced with ensure_binary_response().

scores

Numeric scores or probabilities.

selected

Ignored; kept for signature compatibility.

difficulty

Factor or character vector of "easy" / "hard" labels, same length as truth. Must be supplied.

cutoff_prob

Classification probability cutoff applied to scores. Ignored when cutoff_strategy is not "fixed".

cutoff_strategy

Strategy for computing cutoff. One of "fixed" (use cutoff_prob), "prevalence" (cutoff = class prevalence), or "youden" (optimal Youden's J). Default is "fixed".

positive

Label treated as the positive ("event") class.

Value

Balanced accuracy across easy/hard strata, between 0 and 1. Returns NA_real_ if classification is undefined in both strata.

Details

The difficulty vector must be supplied via the params argument of define_objectives() or build_objectives():

define_objectives(
  metrics = c("easy_hard_accuracy", "num_features"),
  params = list(easy_hard_accuracy = list(difficulty = sample_labels))
)

Note

The difficulty vector is captured at objective-definition time. This works with optimize_panel() which evaluates on the full pooled training data. For optimize_panel_transferable(), which subsets data into train/validation partitions, the difficulty vector would be misaligned with the subsetted truth—use only with the standard pipeline.
